description: Building interactive applications: App Designer, the uifigure component family (buttons, fields, tables, layouts, panels and gauges), modal dialogs and progress indicators, file and folder selection dialogs, and the legacy uicontrol-based interface still found in older code.

tools.name: appdesigner
tools.description: Opens App Designer, the integrated environment for building MATLAB apps with a drag-and-drop canvas and a code view backed by a generated classdef. Apps are saved as .mlapp files and can be run from the Apps tab, from the command line by name, or packaged as standalone applications. Use it for anything beyond a trivial dialog.
tools.usage:
appdesigner
appdesigner(filename)
appdesigner('new')
tools.example:
appdesigner
appdesigner('myApp.mlapp')
% Run a saved app from the command line:
% app = myApp;
% delete(app)
tools.notes: The .mlapp file is a zip container holding both the layout and the class code, so it cannot be usefully diffed by ordinary version control tools. Startup logic goes in the StartupFcn callback, and shared state belongs in private properties of the app class.

tools.name: uifigure
tools.description: Creates a figure window configured for app building, using the web-based graphics system that all ui* components require. It differs from `figure` in the components it accepts, the dialogs it supports and its rendering pipeline. Use it as the container when building an app programmatically.
tools.usage:
fig = uifigure
fig = uifigure(Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Icon'
parameters.description: Path to a window icon image.

tools.notes: Components created with the ui* functions require a uifigure parent; placing them in a plain `figure` errors. Conversely `plot` into a uifigure needs a `uiaxes`, not the classic `axes`.

tools.name: uigridlayout
tools.description: Creates a grid layout manager that positions child components in rows and columns, resizing them automatically when the window changes size. Row and column sizes can be fixed pixels, proportional weights ('1x') or 'fit'. Use it instead of pixel positions for any app that should resize gracefully.
tools.usage:
g = uigridlayout(parent)
g = uigridlayout(parent, [nrows ncols])
g = uigridlayout(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'RowHeight', 'ColumnWidth'
parameters.description: Cell arrays mixing pixel values, '1x' weights and 'fit'.

parameters.name: 'Padding'
parameters.description: [left bottom right top] margins in pixels.

parameters.name: child.Layout.Row / .Column
parameters.description: Set on each child to place it, with a two-element vector to span cells.

parameters.name: 'Scrollable'
parameters.description: 'on' to add scrollbars when content overflows.

tools.notes: A child placed in a grid layout ignores its Position property entirely; use Layout.Row and Layout.Column. Nesting grid layouts is the standard way to build complex responsive interfaces.

tools.name: uiaxes
tools.description: Creates axes suitable for plotting inside a uifigure or App Designer app. Most plotting functions accept a uiaxes handle as their first argument. Use it to embed charts in an app, remembering that the current-axes functions such as `gca` and `hold on` without a handle do not apply.
tools.usage:
ax = uiaxes(parent)
ax = uiaxes(parent, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Position'
parameters.description: Pixel position when not in a layout.

tools.notes: Always pass the axes handle explicitly to plotting, `hold`, `title` and `legend`; inside an app there is no meaningful current axes. A few older plotting functions do not support uiaxes and require a classic figure.

tools.name: uibutton
tools.description: Creates a push button or a state (toggle) button in a uifigure, with text, an icon and a callback that runs when it is pressed. Use push buttons for actions and state buttons for on/off modes. The callback receives the component and an event data object.
tools.usage:
btn = uibutton(parent)
btn = uibutton(parent, style)
btn = uibutton(___, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Callbacks take (source, eventData) arguments; an anonymous function that ignores them is written `@(~,~) doSomething()`. Disable a button with Enable 'off' while a long operation runs to prevent re-entrant calls.

tools.name: uilabel
tools.description: Creates a static text label for captions, field names and status messages in a uifigure. Text can be a character vector, a string, or a cell array for multiple lines, and supports HTML-like formatting through the Interpreter property. Use labels to name every input so the app is self-explanatory.
tools.usage:
lbl = uilabel(parent)
lbl = uilabel(parent, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Text'
parameters.description: Label content; a cell array gives multiple lines.

parameters.name: 'HorizontalAlignment', 'VerticalAlignment'
parameters.description: Text alignment within the label box.

tools.notes: Labels that may hold long messages need 'WordWrap' set to 'on', otherwise the text is clipped. Updating a status label inside a loop requires `drawnow` for the change to appear.

tools.name: uieditfield
tools.description: Creates a text or numeric entry field. The numeric style validates input automatically, enforces Limits, and can display values with a chosen format, which removes most manual input checking. Use ValueChangedFcn to react when the user commits a value.
tools.usage:
fld = uieditfield(parent)
fld = uieditfield(parent, style)
fld = uieditfield(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Limits'
parameters.description: Two-element allowed range for numeric fields.

parameters.name: 'ValueDisplayFormat'
parameters.description: sprintf-style format for numeric display, for example '%.2f Hz'.

parameters.name: 'ValueChangedFcn', 'ValueChangingFcn'
parameters.description: Callbacks on commit and while typing.

tools.notes: Numeric fields reject out-of-range entries and restore the previous value automatically, so no extra validation is needed. The event data carries both Value and PreviousValue, which is useful for undo and logging.

tools.name: uidropdown
tools.description: Creates a drop-down list for choosing one item from a set, with separate display Items and underlying ItemsData values. Setting ItemsData lets the callback receive a code or object rather than the displayed text. The Editable property allows free text entry in addition to the list.
tools.usage:
dd = uidropdown(parent)
dd = uidropdown(parent, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Items'
parameters.description: Cell or string array of displayed options.

parameters.name: 'ItemsData'
parameters.description: Values associated with each item, returned in Value.

parameters.name: 'Value'
parameters.description: Currently selected item or item data.

parameters.name: 'Editable'
parameters.description: 'on' to allow typing a value not in the list.

tools.notes: When ItemsData is set, the Value property holds the data value rather than the displayed text, which is what callbacks should use. Assigning a new Items list resets Value to the first item unless you set it explicitly afterwards.

tools.name: uilistbox
tools.description: Creates a list box showing several items at once, with optional multiple selection. Like the drop-down it supports ItemsData for separating display text from underlying values. Use it when the user must see the available options or select several of them.
tools.usage:
lb = uilistbox(parent)
lb = uilistbox(parent, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Value'
parameters.description: Selected item or, with multiselect, a cell array of them.

tools.notes: With Multiselect on, Value is always a cell array even when one item is selected, so code must handle both shapes if the property is toggled. Very long lists are better served by a `uitable` with filtering.

tools.name: uicheckbox
tools.description: Creates a check box representing an independent on/off option, with a logical Value property. Use it for settings that are not mutually exclusive; use radio buttons in a button group for exclusive choices. The ValueChangedFcn callback receives the new state.
tools.usage:
cbx = uicheckbox(parent)
cbx = uicheckbox(parent, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Value is a logical, so it can be used directly in `if` statements. Enabling and disabling dependent controls from the callback keeps the interface consistent with the option state.

tools.name: uiswitch
tools.description: Creates a switch component in slider, rocker or toggle style, representing a two-state choice with named positions. Value is the text of the selected position rather than a logical. Use it in instrument-style interfaces where a switch metaphor is clearer than a check box.
tools.usage:
sw = uiswitch(parent)
sw = uiswitch(parent, style)
sw = uiswitch(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Items'
parameters.description: Two-element cell array of position labels.

parameters.name: 'ItemsData'
parameters.description: Values associated with the two positions.

tools.notes: Without ItemsData, Value is the label text, so comparisons must use `strcmp`; setting ItemsData to logicals makes the callback code much cleaner. `uilamp` is the usual companion indicator.

tools.name: uislider
tools.description: Creates a slider for selecting a value from a continuous range, with configurable limits, major and minor tick marks and labels. Two callbacks are available: one on release and one continuously while dragging. Use it for parameters the user wants to explore interactively.
tools.usage:
sld = uislider(parent)
sld = uislider(parent, style)
sld = uislider(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: 'slider' (default) or 'range' for a two-handle slider (R2023b and later).

parameters.name: 'ValueChangedFcn'
parameters.description: Callback when the user releases the slider.

tools.notes: Use ValueChangingFcn for live preview, but keep the callback fast because it fires many times per second. The event data field is `e.Value` during dragging, not `s.Value`, which only updates on release.

tools.name: uispinner
tools.description: Creates a numeric spinner with up and down arrows and direct typing, enforcing limits and a step size. Use it for integer or quantized parameters where a slider is too imprecise and a plain field too permissive. Rounding and display formatting are configurable.
tools.usage:
spn = uispinner(parent)
spn = uispinner(parent, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Setting RoundFractionalValues to 'on' is essential for parameters that must be integers, otherwise typed input can be fractional. Limits are enforced for both typed and stepped values.

tools.name: uitable
tools.description: Displays tabular data in a grid that can be made editable, sortable and individually styled. Data can be a MATLAB table, a numeric matrix or a cell array, with the table form giving automatic column names and types. Use it for data entry, for reviewing results and for building simple spreadsheet-like interfaces.
tools.usage:
t = uitable(parent)
t = uitable(parent, Name, Value)
addStyle(t, style, target, index)
removeStyle(t)

parameters.name: 'Data'
parameters.description: Table, matrix or cell array to display.

parameters.name: 'ColumnEditable'
parameters.description: Logical array controlling which columns can be edited.

tools.notes: Editing updates the Data property in place, so read `src.Data` in the callback to get the current state. Very large tables render slowly; page the data or filter before display.

tools.name: uipanel
tools.description: Creates a panel that groups related components inside a border with an optional title, and can be made scrollable. Children are positioned relative to the panel, so moving the panel moves everything in it. Use panels to structure an interface visually and to show or hide whole sections at once.
tools.usage:
p = uipanel(parent)
p = uipanel(parent, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Child positions are relative to the panel's lower-left corner, not the figure. Toggling a panel's Visible property is the easiest way to switch between modes of an interface.

tools.name: uitabgroup
tools.description: Creates a container of tabs, each created with `uitab`, that shows one page of content at a time. Use it to organize an app with several distinct views without opening extra windows. The SelectionChangedFcn callback fires when the user switches tabs.
tools.usage:
tg = uitabgroup(parent)
tg = uitabgroup(parent, Name, Value)
tab = uitab(tg, 'Title', txt)

parameters.name: 'SelectedTab'
parameters.description: Handle of the currently shown tab.

parameters.name: 'SelectionChangedFcn'
parameters.description: Callback when the active tab changes.

tools.notes: Components in a hidden tab still exist and can be updated, but drawing into them is wasted work; defer expensive plotting to the SelectionChangedFcn. Tabs accept the same children as a panel.

tools.name: uigauge
tools.description: Creates a gauge in circular, semicircular, linear or ninety-degree style for displaying a value within a range, with coloured scale bands. Use it in monitoring dashboards where a quick visual reading matters more than precision. Scale colours highlight normal, warning and alarm regions.
tools.usage:
g = uigauge(parent)
g = uigauge(parent, style)
g = uigauge(___, Name, Value)
tools.notes: ScaleColorLimits must be an n-by-2 matrix whose rows match the ScaleColors entries. Updating a gauge in a tight loop needs `drawnow` for the needle to move.

tools.name: uiknob
tools.description: Creates a rotary knob for continuous values or a discrete knob for selecting one of several labelled positions. Use it for instrument-style interfaces where a knob metaphor suits the task. It supports both ValueChangedFcn and continuous ValueChangingFcn callbacks.
tools.usage:
knob = uiknob(parent)
knob = uiknob(parent, style)
knob = uiknob(___, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Discrete knobs snap to their Items and return the label text unless ItemsData is set. As with sliders, use `e.Value` in ValueChangingFcn rather than `s.Value`.

tools.name: uialert
tools.description: Displays a modal message dialog attached to a uifigure, with an icon indicating error, warning, information or success. It is non-blocking by default, returning immediately while the dialog stays on screen. Use it to report errors and completion from within an app.
tools.usage:
uialert(fig, message, title)
uialert(fig, message, title, Name, Value)

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Text to display; a cell array gives several lines.

parameters.name: 'Modal'
parameters.description: true (default) blocks interaction with the app window.

parameters.name: 'CloseFcn'
parameters.description: Callback invoked when the dialog closes.

tools.notes: uialert requires a uifigure parent and does not work with a classic `figure`; use `errordlg` or `msgbox` there. Because it returns immediately, put follow-up work in the CloseFcn callback.

tools.name: uiconfirm
tools.description: Displays a modal confirmation dialog in a uifigure with customizable buttons, returning the user's choice. It can block and return the selection directly, or invoke a callback when closed. Use it before destructive actions and for yes/no decisions inside an app.
tools.usage:
selection = uiconfirm(fig, message, title)
selection = uiconfirm(fig, message, title, Name, Value)
uiconfirm(___, 'CloseFcn', fcn)

parameters.name: 'DefaultOption'
parameters.description: Index or label of the default button.

parameters.name: 'CancelOption'
parameters.description: Button treated as cancel, also used when the dialog is dismissed.

parameters.name: 'CloseFcn'
parameters.description: Callback receiving the selection; makes the call non-blocking.

tools.notes: Setting CancelOption ensures that closing the dialog with the window control returns a safe answer. The blocking form must not be used inside a callback that also needs to keep the interface responsive; use CloseFcn instead.

tools.name: uiprogressdlg
tools.description: Creates a progress dialog in a uifigure, either determinate with a value from 0 to 1 or indeterminate for unknown-length work. A cancel button can be enabled and polled through the CancelRequested property. Use it to keep the user informed during long computations.
tools.usage:
d = uiprogressdlg(fig)
d = uiprogressdlg(fig, Name, Value)
d.Value = v;
close(d)

parameters.name: 'Indeterminate'
parameters.description: 'on' for an animated bar of unknown length.

parameters.name: 'CancelRequested'
parameters.description: Read-only property that becomes true when cancel is pressed.

tools.notes: You must close the dialog yourself; wrapping the close in `onCleanup` guarantees it disappears even if the loop errors. Check CancelRequested regularly, since cancelling only sets the flag and does not interrupt the loop.

tools.name: uigetfile
tools.description: Opens a modal dialog for selecting one or more existing files, returning the file name and folder, or 0 when the user cancels. File type filters control what is shown and offered. Use it in interactive tools to let the user choose input files.
tools.usage:
[file, path] = uigetfile
[file, path] = uigetfile(filter)
[file, path] = uigetfile(filter, title)
[file, path] = uigetfile(filter, title, defname)
[file, path, idx] = uigetfile(___, 'MultiSelect', 'on')

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Pattern such as '*.csv', or an n-by-2 cell array of patterns and descriptions.

parameters.name: defname
parameters.description: Default file name or starting folder.

tools.notes: Always test the returned file against 0 before using it, since cancelling returns the numeric 0 rather than an empty string. With MultiSelect on, `file` is a cell array when several files are chosen and a character vector when only one is.

tools.name: uiputfile
tools.description: Opens a modal Save As dialog for choosing an output file name and folder, prompting about overwriting an existing file. It returns 0 if the user cancels. Use it when an interactive tool needs a destination for exported results.
tools.usage:
[file, path] = uiputfile
[file, path] = uiputfile(filter)
[file, path] = uiputfile(filter, title)
[file, path, idx] = uiputfile(filter, title, defname)

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: File pattern or cell array of patterns and descriptions.

tools.notes: The dialog asks about overwriting, but it does not create or lock the file, so a race is still possible in multi-process use. As with `uigetfile`, cancellation returns 0.

tools.name: uigetdir
tools.description: Opens a modal dialog for choosing a folder, returning its full path or 0 when cancelled. Use it when a tool processes every file in a directory chosen by the user. A starting folder and a prompt can be supplied.
tools.usage:
folder = uigetdir
folder = uigetdir(startPath)
folder = uigetdir(startPath, title)

parameters.name: startPath
parameters.description: Folder to open the dialog in.

tools.notes: The return value is a character vector on success and the numeric 0 on cancel, so test with `isequal(folder, 0)` rather than `isempty`. The dialog does not create folders; use `mkdir` afterwards if needed.

tools.name: inputdlg
tools.description: Displays a modal dialog with one or more text entry fields and returns the answers as a cell array of character vectors, or an empty cell if cancelled. Use it for quick parameter prompts in scripts that do not justify a full app. All answers come back as text and must be converted.
tools.usage:
answer = inputdlg(prompt)
answer = inputdlg(prompt, dlgtitle)
answer = inputdlg(prompt, dlgtitle, dims)
answer = inputdlg(prompt, dlgtitle, dims, definput)
answer = inputdlg(___, opts)

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Cell array of prompt strings, one per field.

parameters.name: dims
parameters.description: Field size in rows, or an n-by-2 matrix of [rows columns].

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: 'on' for resizable, or a struct with Resize, WindowStyle and Interpreter fields.

tools.notes: Cancelling returns an empty cell array, so always check with `isempty` before indexing. Because everything is text, validate with `str2double` and check for NaN.

tools.name: msgbox
tools.description: Displays a simple message dialog with an optional icon, returning the dialog handle. By default it is non-modal, so execution continues immediately. Use it in scripts and classic figure-based tools; inside a uifigure app use `uialert` instead.
tools.usage:
msgbox(message)
msgbox(message, title)
msgbox(message, title, icon)
msgbox(___, createmode)
f = msgbox(___)
tools.notes: Because the default is non-modal, the script continues while the box is open; wrap it in `uiwait` when you need to block. `errordlg`, `warndlg` and `helpdlg` are preconfigured variants.

tools.name: questdlg
tools.description: Displays a modal question dialog with up to three custom buttons and returns the label of the one pressed, or an empty character vector if the dialog is dismissed. Use it for yes/no/cancel decisions in scripts and classic figure tools. Inside a uifigure app, `uiconfirm` is the equivalent.
tools.usage:
answer = questdlg(question)
answer = questdlg(question, title)
answer = questdlg(question, title, default)
answer = questdlg(question, title, btn1, btn2, default)
answer = questdlg(question, title, btn1, btn2, btn3, default)
tools.notes: Dismissing the dialog with the window close button returns an empty character vector, which the `otherwise` branch must handle. Always set an explicit default so pressing Enter does something safe.

tools.name: listdlg
tools.description: Displays a modal list selection dialog and returns the indices of the chosen items plus a flag indicating whether OK was pressed. Single or multiple selection modes are available. Use it to let a user pick from a computed list of files, variables or options.
tools.usage:
[indx, tf] = listdlg('ListString', list)
[indx, tf] = listdlg('ListString', list, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'ListString'
parameters.description: Cell or string array of items to display.

parameters.name: 'InitialValue'
parameters.description: Indices selected when the dialog opens.

parameters.name: 'ListSize'
parameters.description: [width height] of the list in pixels.

tools.notes: The second output is 0 when the user cancels, and the index output is empty then, so check it before indexing. Items are plain text, so keep a parallel array if you need associated data.

tools.name: waitbar
tools.description: Creates and updates a progress bar in a classic figure window, with an optional cancel button implemented through a callback. Use it in scripts and legacy tools; in a uifigure app use `uiprogressdlg`. Update it by passing the existing handle rather than creating a new bar each iteration.
tools.usage:
f = waitbar(x)
f = waitbar(x, msg)
waitbar(x, f)
waitbar(x, f, msg)
f = waitbar(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'CreateCancelBtn'
parameters.description: Callback that runs when the cancel button is pressed.

tools.notes: Creating a new waitbar inside the loop instead of updating the existing handle opens dozens of windows. Updating it every iteration of a fast loop dominates the run time, so update every few percent instead.

tools.name: uicontrol
tools.description: Creates a classic user interface control (push button, edit box, slider, list box, check box, radio button, popup menu or static text) in a traditional figure. This is the pre-App Designer interface, still widely present in older code and required when components must live in a plain `figure`. New apps should use the ui* component family in a uifigure.
tools.usage:
c = uicontrol
c = uicontrol(parent)
c = uicontrol(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Position'
parameters.description: [left bottom width height] in the units of the Units property.

parameters.name: 'Callback'
parameters.description: Function executed when the control is used.

parameters.name: 'Value', 'Min', 'Max'
parameters.description: State and range, whose meaning depends on the style.

tools.notes: GUIDE, the graphical editor that generated uicontrol-based apps, has been removed from recent releases; MathWorks provides a migration tool that converts GUIDE apps to App Designer. uicontrol components cannot be placed in a uifigure.

tools.name: uimenu
tools.description: Creates menus and menu items in a figure's menu bar, or submenu items under an existing menu. Each item has a callback, an optional keyboard accelerator and a separator flag. Use it to give an app a conventional File and Edit menu structure.
tools.usage:
m = uimenu
m = uimenu(parent)
m = uimenu(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Text'
parameters.description: Menu label; an ampersand marks the mnemonic character.

parameters.name: 'MenuSelectedFcn'
parameters.description: Callback executed when the item is chosen.

parameters.name: 'Accelerator'
parameters.description: Single character used with the platform modifier key.

parameters.name: 'Separator'
parameters.description: 'on' to draw a divider above the item.

tools.notes: `uimenu` works in both classic figures and uifigures. For right-click menus use `uicontextmenu` together with the ContextMenu property of the target component.

tools.name: uiwait
tools.description: Blocks execution until a figure is closed, until `uiresume` is called on it, or until a timeout expires. Use it to make a custom dialog modal and to pause a script until the user has finished interacting. `uiresume` releases the wait from a callback.
tools.usage:
uiwait
uiwait(fig)
uiwait(fig, timeout)
uiresume(fig)

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum number of seconds to wait.

tools.notes: After uiwait returns, the figure may have been deleted, so check `isvalid` before using its handle or reading data from it. A callback that never calls `uiresume` leaves the script blocked until the window is closed.
